title: Semilinear Frobenius transport and explicit field-operation lifts
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius, and $P_T=Lg_T^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use the rational/common-stage bounded constructible categories and Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:P_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$, whose arrows satisfy $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_T(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and put $f=f_0\times_{k_0}k:X\to Y$. The square $fg_X=g_Yf$ is Cartesian as a square of schemes; to view it over $k$, its source corners have structural maps $a_Tg_T$. The functors $P_T$ are exact equivalences, inverse to pullback along $g_T^{-1}$, on these field coefficient categories. Their integral realization is the exact inverse-image transport on completed coefficient modules; the inverse-composition identities survive scalar localization and the common-finite-field construction.

For each covariant operation $F\in\{Lf^*,Rf_*,Rf_!\}$ on a domain where the underlying functor preserves bounded constructibility, let $a:P_{\mathrm{out}}F\xrightarrow{\sim}FP_{\mathrm{in}}$ be its canonical Frobenius comparison. The rule
$$ (K,\theta_K)\longmapsto(FK,F(\theta_K)a_K),\qquad u\longmapsto F(u) $$
is a functor on Weil pairs, and on Weil arrows it satisfies
$$ F(u)F(\theta_K)a_K=F(\theta_L)a_LP_{\mathrm{out}}(F(u)). $$
Here $Rf_!$ is the compact-support functor of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], with its field-coefficient passage as specified in [def-exchange-projection], and $Rf_*$ is [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. In particular $a=\operatorname{Ex}_*$ or $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ gives the specified direct-image structure. For $W=X,Y$, the tensor and internal-Hom structures are respectively
$$ (\theta_M\otimes\theta_N)\mu_g,\qquad R\mathcal Hom(\theta_M^{-1},\theta_N)h_g, $$
where $\mu_g:P_W(M\otimes^LN)\simeq P_WM\otimes^LP_WN$ and $h_g:P_WR\mathcal Hom(M,N)\simeq R\mathcal Hom(P_WM,P_WN)$ are the canonical transport comparisons. These formulas define functors, covariant in both tensor arguments and contravariant in the first Hom argument, on each already-proved constructible domain. In particular retain $M\in D^b_{ctf}$, $N\in D^b_c$ and any site-perfect first-variable restriction [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Forgetting recovers the given objects and arrows of all five operations. Exactness is that of their underlying derived functors; this asserts neither larger constructibility domains nor a triangulated structure on Weil pairs.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian], $g_X,g_Y$ are scheme isomorphisms, $fg_X=g_Yf$, and the displayed square is Cartesian. This does not assert $k$-linearity. Indeed, if $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the usual structure map, the upper copy of $T$ has structure map $a_Tg_T$; then $g_T$ is a map to the lower copy over $k$, and $a_Yg_Yf=a_Xg_X$ makes the left vertical arrow a map over $k$. These are precisely the restructured source corners in the assertion.

Apply lem-pod-isomorphism-field-transport to geometric Frobenius. Its stage records supply both normalized integral epsilon equations, their rationalizations, exactness and equivalence. Its common-stage records supply the inverse identities and their finite-field inclusion formulas. The termwise realization is lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback; exact completed module transport is also recorded in lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation. These give PodRationalFrobeniusTransportSpec and the transport clauses on both models.

source.place: Sentence 1, expanded by lem-fix-weil-operations.proof.md, first paragraph; re-split of original Steps 2–3

proof.text: Build the rational square from the canonical rationalized integral compositors. Naturality on a pure tensor is integral compositor naturality, and tensor induction gives every rational arrow. For the common-stage compositors, use the defining representative equations of def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom and lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso. Represent an arrow over one field, compose representatives and cancel transition comparisons. The remaining equality is rational compositor naturality. Compose the inverse first compositor, the equality of scheme maps and the second compositor to obtain exactly the specified square components. On a supplied operation stage, apply lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences to the ordinary square and its proper factor. The compactification exchange is a composite of this invertible proper mate, the supplied open base-change isomorphism and the supplied compactification identifications. Thus the stipulated exchange maps themselves are invertible.

source.place: Sentence 1, expanded by lem-fix-weil-operations.proof.md, first paragraph; re-split of original Steps 4–5

proof.text: Put $\Theta_K=F(\theta_K)a_K$. For a Weil arrow, $F(u)\Theta_K=F(u\theta_K)a_K=F(\theta_L)F(P_{\rm in}u)a_K=F(\theta_L)a_LP_{\rm out}(F(u))$ by naturality. Both factors of $\Theta$ are invertible. Arrows of pairs are equal iff their underlying arrows are, and the underlying functor preserves identities and composition, proving the three lifts by [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].

source.place: Sentence 1, expanded by lem-fix-weil-operations.proof.md, first paragraph; original Step 6

proof.text: Use $\mu$ of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] and set $\Theta_{M,N}=(\theta_M\otimes\theta_N)\mu$, invertible since $\theta_M,\theta_N,\mu$ are. For Weil arrows $u,v$, $(u\otimes v)\Theta=(u\theta_M\otimes v\theta_N)\mu=(\theta_{M\prime}\otimes\theta_{N\prime})(Pu\otimes Pv)\mu=\Theta_{M\prime,N\prime}P(u\otimes v)$. The tensor bifunctor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] supplies identity and composition laws.

source.place: Sentence 1, expanded by lem-fix-weil-operations.proof.md, first paragraph; original Step 7

proof.text: Write $H=R\mathcal Hom$ and use $h:PH(M,N)\simeq H(PM,PN)$ from [lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation], at the field stages on the pairs of the item, whose internal Hom is constructible. Put $\Theta=H(\theta_M^{-1},\theta_N)h$, an isomorphism. For Weil arrows $u:M\prime\to M$, $v:N\to N\prime$, the arrow equations give $\theta_M^{-1}u=Pu\,\theta_{M\prime}^{-1}$ and $v\theta_N=\theta_{N\prime}Pv$. Hence $H(u,v)\Theta=H(\theta_M^{-1}u,v\theta_N)h=H(\theta_{M\prime}^{-1},\theta_{N\prime})H(Pu,Pv)h=\Theta_{M\prime,N\prime}P(H(u,v))$. The bifunctor laws of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give identities and composition; the first inverse has the required type $M\to PM$.

source.place: Sentence 1, expanded by lem-fix-weil-operations.proof.md, first paragraph; original Step 8

proof.text: The forgetful functor [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] recovers every stipulated object and arrow. All constructions stay in the already preserved domains, retaining finite-Tor and site-perfect restrictions. No underlying functor, shift comparison or triangle changes, so exactness is the underlying derived exactness, in each covariant variable and contravariantly in the first Hom variable, with no triangulation asserted for pairs.
